brief.ask: Create a brand identity for Seamline, the open-source command-line tool in this folder.
brief.owner: Owner preferences: precise, trustworthy, developer-native; it must work in a terminal-heavy README, as a GitHub avatar and on a small docs site. No database cylinders, no elephants, no generic terminal prompt. Web and GitHub only.

claim.notes: No concept passed the quality gate: through-line and stepped-path got 'none' in two sketch reviews, and offset-s failed the critic gate in both rounds (6.54 then 5.85, present=no), so nothing was finalized, exported or installed and no gallery was built.

concepts.title: Offset S
readsAs: heavy S/3 with a slash through it
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s1 an S whose two hooks slip past each other; s2 a blocky 5 or S; s3 a sliced S (common trope); s4 a 5 with orange bar, UI-ish; s5 a striped S, dies at 16px. Keep s1: only one with a real seam in the counter and clean at 16px. Fix: it risks reading as a cut-S trope, so make the offset the memorable gesture (stronger asymmetry, one deliberate gap) and keep it single colour. Judgment.

concepts.title: Stepped Path
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s1 blocky Z/S letter or flag; s2 prohibited sign/coffee bean/pill; s3 letter X or hourglass; s4 C+D letter pair or yin-yang. Handover gap works only in s4 and s1 but each reads as a letter first, and s1 is stair-like. Different move: drop the track metaphor; use a single asymmetric seam-cut form that is not a letter, disc or ring.

concepts.title: Through Line
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s1 speed bump/arch/tilde-caret; s2 stair-step or pipe bend (forbidden stairs); s3 pill capsule or 'i', gone at 16px; s4 letter O/6; s5 letter S. All generic line-wiggles; the one-line idea is not ownable. Try a different move: a mark built from the seam itself (a negative-space cut that is the only thing that differs between two identical halves), not a path drawn as a stroke.
